source.title: COMPARATIVE PRIME NUMBER THEORY PROBLEM LIST

accepted.question_text: Let an ordinate of an L-function mean the positive imaginary part of a nontrivial zero of that L-function. Prove that the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) has at least one positive ordinate that is irrational.

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Prove that ζ(s) has at least one(!) irrational ordinate.

accepted.question_text: Let the positive ordinates of ζ(s) denote the positive imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Prove that these positive ordinates are not all rational multiples of one another.

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Prove that the positive ordinates of ζ(s) are not all rational multiples of one another.

accepted.question_text: For nontrivial zeros ρ of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s), obtain upper bounds for the quantity 1/|ζ′(ρ)| as ρ ranges over those zeros.

evidence.quote: Problem: Can we obtain upper bounds for 1/|ζ ′(ρ)| as ρ runs over the nontrivial zeros of ζ(s)?

accepted.question_text: Assume the simple zeros conjecture for ζ(s) and the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble conjecture for nearest-neighbour spacing of its zeros. Using formula (1) in the paper for 1/ζ′(ρ), compute an upper bound for the moment sum Σ_{0<γ<T} 1/|ζ′(ρ)|^{2k} for positive real k, with special interest in k = 1/2 and k = 1, where ρ = 1/2 + iγ runs over nontrivial zeros of ζ(s).
accepted.context_brief: conditional upper bounds for zeta-derivative moments

evidence.quote: Problem: Use the formula (1) to compute an upper bound for Σ_{0<γ<T} 1/|ζ ′(ρ)|^{2k} for positive real numbers k (the cases k = 1/2 and k = 1 are especially interesting), assuming SZ and the GUE conjecture on the nearest-neighbour spacing on zeros of ζ(s).

accepted.question_text: For nontrivial zeros ρ = 1/2 + iγ of ζ(s), establish lower bounds for moments involving ζ(2ρ)/ζ′(ρ). In particular, use the argument of Milinovich and Ng [30] to prove the lower bound Σ_{0<γ<T} |ζ(2ρ)/ζ′(ρ)|^2 ≥ (1/(4π) + o(1))T, and prove lower bounds for the more general discrete moments Σ_{0<γ<T} |ζ(2ρ)/ζ′(ρ)|^{2k} for positive real k.
accepted.context_brief: lower bounds for zeta ratio moments

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Use the argument in Milinovich and Ng [30] to establish the lower bound Σ_{0<γ<T} |ζ(2ρ)/ζ ′(ρ)|^2 ≥ (1/(4π) + o(1)) T. Problem 2: Prove lower bounds for the discrete moments of the shape Σ_{0<γ<T} |ζ(2ρ)/ζ ′(ρ)|^{2k} ≫ T (log T)^{(k+1)^2}.

accepted.question_text: Let m(ρ) denote the multiplicity of a nontrivial zero ρ of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s). Improve the known upper bounds for m(ρ).

evidence.quote: Problem: Can we improve upper bounds for the multiplicities of nontrivial zeros of ζ(s)?

accepted.question_text: Let q be a modulus and let a and b be distinct reduced residue classes modulo q. Obtain an upper bound, as strong as possible in terms of q, for the first sign change of the prime-number-race difference π(x; q, a) − π(x; q, b).

evidence.quote: Problem: Obtain an upper bound for the first sign change of π(x; q, a) − π(x; q, b) in terms of q, preferably one that increases as slowly as possible.

accepted.question_text: For a number field K with ring of integers O_K, let κ_K be the residue at the pole s = 1 of the Dedekind zeta function ζ_K(s), and define Δ_K(x) = ∏_{N(𝔭)≤x}(1 − 1/N(𝔭))^{-1} − e^γ κ_K log x, where the product runs over prime ideals 𝔭 of O_K with norm N(𝔭) at most x. Localize the first negative value of Δ_K(x) when K is Q(√5), Q(√13), or another simple number field, and more generally obtain an upper bound for the first sign change of Δ_K(x) in a family of number fields K.

evidence.quote: Problem: Localize the first negative value for ∆K(x) when K is Q(√5), Q(√13), or some other simple number field. In general, obtain an upper bound for the first sign change of ∆K(x) for a family of number fields K.

accepted.question_text: In highly biased prime number races, such as the appropriately normalized race between quadratic residues and nonresidues for composite moduli q, bound the associated Skewes numbers in terms of the parameters defining the race, either conjecturally or with proofs.
accepted.context_brief: Skewes numbers for highly biased races

evidence.quote: Problem: Bound Skewes’s numbers of other highly biased races in terms of the parameters defining the race, either conjecturally or provably.

accepted.question_text: In the function-field setting for Chebyshev’s bias, one often assumes both linear independence over Q of the relevant zero arguments and linear independence of those arguments together with π. Show that whenever linear independence with π fails, that failure always has a geometric explanation.
accepted.context_brief: function-field bias and linear independence with pi

evidence.quote: Problem: Show that the failure of linear independence with π always has a geometric explanation.

accepted.question_text: Let f ∈ Z[x,y] be a primitive positive definite binary quadratic form satisfying f(x,1) ≢ x(x+1) (mod 2), and let π_f(x) = #{p ≤ x : p = f(a,b^2) for some integers a and b}. When f and g are distinct such quadratic forms with the same discriminant, determine how π_f(x) and π_g(x) compare as x → ∞. The source also asks for analogous comparison questions for indefinite binary quadratic forms and for primitive binary cubic forms F and G of the same type when π_F(x) ∼ π_G(x).
accepted.context_brief: compare prime counts from quadratic forms

evidence.quote: Problem: If f and g are two distinct such quadratic forms with the same discriminant, how do the quantities πf(x) and πg(x) compare as x → ∞?

accepted.question_text: A new formulation of Chebyshev’s bias considers the weighted prime-counting difference Σ_{p≤x, p≡3 (mod 4)} 1/√p − Σ_{p≤x, p≡1 (mod 4)} 1/√p ∼ (1/2) log log x as x → ∞. Determine the logical inclusion or precise relation between this weighted formulation and the conventional formulation of Chebyshev’s bias in which the set of x satisfying π(x;4,3) > π(x;4,1) has logarithmic density very close to 1.
accepted.context_brief: compare two formulations of Chebyshev bias

evidence.quote: Problem: What is the logical inclusion or relation of this new definition to the conventional definiton of “Chebyshev’s bias” in terms of the logarithmic density of the set of x satisfying π(x, 4, 3) > π(x, 4, 1) being very close to 1?

accepted.question_text: Let q be a modulus and let a and b be distinct reduced residue classes modulo q. Prove unconditionally that the set of real numbers x for which π(x; q, a) = π(x; q, b), meaning the ties in this prime number race, has natural density 0 or logarithmic density 0.
accepted.context_brief: density of ties in prime races

evidence.quote: Problem: Prove unconditionally that the set of x for which π(x; q, a) = π(x; q, b) (the set of “ties” in the prime number race) has (natural or logarithmic) density 0.

accepted.question_text: Define Δ_θ^r(x) = Σ_{p≤x} (log p)/p − (log x + E), where E = −γ − Σ_p log p/(p(p−1)). Find an explicit constant X such that Δ_θ^r(x) < 0 for some x ≤ X.
accepted.context_brief: explicit sign change in Mertens first theorem

evidence.quote: Problem: Find an explicit constant X such that ∆θr(x) < 0 for some x ≤ X.

accepted.question_text: The best known non-explicit unconditional upper bound for the Mertens sum M(x) has the shape M(x) ≪ x exp(−C (log x)^{3/5} (log log x)^{−1/5}). Find an explicit version of this bound, which would sharpen explicit upper bounds for M(x) at large x.

evidence.quote: Problem: Find an explicit version of this upper bound, which would thus give a sharper bound for M(x) for large x.

accepted.question_text: Define S(x) = Σ_{n≤x} (−2)^{Ω(n)}, where Ω(n) counts prime factors with multiplicity, and define α = lim sup_{x→∞} |S(x)|/x. Determine the exact value of α.

evidence.quote: Problem: What is the exact value of α?

accepted.question_text: Let W_ψ(T) be the sign-change counting function associated with the error term ψ(x) − x. Improve the known lower bound for lim inf W_ψ(T)/log T, even under RH if needed, and make progress on understanding sign changes beyond repeated-averaging techniques. The source suggests targets such as 1.01·γ₁/π, 2·γ₁/π, or even an unbounded lim inf.

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Improve this lower bound, even assuming RH. Here are some suggested target lower bounds for lim inf W ψ(T )/log T : (a) 1.01 γ1/π ; (b) 2 γ1/π ; (c) ∞. Problem 2 : Make any progress whatsoever towards advancing our knowledge of sign changes beyond the repeated-averaging techniques.

accepted.question_text: Let P⁺(n) denote the largest prime factor of n, and let χ_{−4} be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo 4. Prove or disprove that Σ_{n≤x} χ_{−4}(P⁺(n)) < 0 for all x ≥ 2, and if possible determine an asymptotic formula for this sum.

evidence.quote: Problem: Prove or disprove that Σ_{n≤x} χ−4(P +(n)) < 0 for all n ≥ 2. Possibly even find an asymptotic formula for the sum.

accepted.question_text: For prime number races with three or more competitors, numerically compute additional three-way or higher-order race densities, and determine a list such as the 100 most biased three-way races.

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Numerically compute some further three-way (or higher) races. Problem 2: Determine the 100 (for example) most biased three-way races.

accepted.question_text: Assuming GRH and LI, compute the logarithmic densities in the five-way prime race among the quadratic residues {1,3,4,5,9} modulo 11 and likewise among the quadratic nonresidues {2,6,7,8,10} modulo 11. The source notes that symmetry reduces the computation to eight representative densities of the form δ_{11;a1,a2,a3,a4,a5}.

evidence.quote: Problem: Compute (assuming GRH and LI) the densities in the five-way race among the quadratic residues and among the quadratic nonresidues modulo 11.

accepted.question_text: Investigate additional numerical examples of prime number races arising from Chebotarev’s density theorem, and determine which two-way Chebotarev races are the most biased.

evidence.quote: Problem: Investigate further examples. Determine the most biased two-way Chebotarev races.

accepted.question_text: Assuming GRH and LI, calculate the logarithmic densities of the sets {n ≥ 1 : (−1)^{Ω(n)}χ_{−4}(n) = 1} and {n ≥ 1 : (−1)^{Ω(n)}χ_{−4}(n) = −1}, where Ω(n) is the number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity and χ_{−4} is the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo 4.

evidence.quote: Problem: Assuming GRH and LI, calculate the logarithmic density of the sets {n ≥ 1: (−1)Ω(n)χ−4(n) = 1} and {n ≥ 1: (−1)Ω(n)χ−4(n) = −1}.

accepted.question_text: For the averaged prime-counting error A_π^1(x; q, a) = ∫_0^x (φ(q)π(t; q, a) − li(t)) dt, classify, under GRH, those pairs (q,a) for which A_π^1(x; q, a) < 0 for all sufficiently large x.
accepted.context_brief: classification of averaged bias by modulus

evidence.quote: Problem: Assuming GRH, classify those values of q and a such that Aπ1(x; q, a) < 0 for all sufficiently large x.
